newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: SOCCER-EL KASS SEEKS PERSONAL AFRICAN CUP GLORY.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-EL KASS SEEKS PERSONAL AFRICAN CUP GLORY.

text.p: Egyptian veteran Ahmed El Kass begins a personal quest in the twilight of his career when Cairo club Zamalek meet Shooting Stars of Nigeria in the first leg of the African Champions' Cup final this weekend.

The 32-year-old midfielder's quick turn of pace has made him one of Africa's leading footballers but it is only late in his playing days that the national team captain is set to win honours at club level.

El Kass spent much of his playing career with unfashionable Alexandria club Olympic before his controversial transfer to Zamalek last year and now gets a chance to win a continental cup medal in his very first African cup campaign.
He also returns to the Zamalek midfield after a two-match suspension, picked up after being sent off in the quarter-finals against COD Meknes of Morocco.
Zamalek, seeking a record fourth African Champions' Cup, are away at Stars' home ground in Ibadan for the first leg on Saturday but will still be overwhelming favourites.
It is the second time these two teams have met in the final, with Zamalek taking a 2-0 aggregate triumph 12 years ago.

This is only the fourth time that a Nigerian club have reached the final of Africa's leading club competition and despite the giant west African country's dominance of continental soccer at all other levels, have been unable to produce a Champions' Cup winner.
Nigeria's last finalists were Iwuanyanwu Nationale, who suffered an embarrasing 4-1 aggregate defeat by Algerian provincial club Entente Setif in 1988.
There will be an Algerian interest in this year's final, too, with Algerian internatinal winger Kamel Kaci Said leading Zamalek's attack.

The Cairo aristocrats boast two veterans of the 1990 World Cup finals in Italy with El Kass and Ismail Youssef still playing key roles in the midfield. Eight other players, including several who have been on the bench of late, are Egyptian internationls.
In contrast, their Nigerian opponents have just midfielder Sam Pam junior with full international honours, and then just a single cap won almost two years ago.
But Stars have proved to be a stubborn team at home and will be seeking to rattle Zamalek before their second leg in Cairo on December 13.
Kawkab Marrakesh will attempt to boost flagging morale for their Confederation of African Football (CAF) Cup second leg tie against holders Etoile du Sahel on Sunday.

The Moroccan team outplayed their Tunisian hosts in the first leg in Sousse earlier this month but still came away with a 3-1 defeat -- several goalkeeping errors proving costly in a 10-minute spell before halftime.
Sahel are attempting to become the first team to win back-to-back CAF Cup titles.
